title: Why a double rainbow has its colours flipped
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why are the colours of a double rainbow upside down?
Why is the second rainbow fainter?
Why is the sky darker between two rainbows?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: The extra bounce flips the colour order

explain.say: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines into raindrops behind you. In each drop the light bends, splits into colours, reflects once off the back, and comes out towards you.

draw.text: Why a double rainbow has its colours flipped

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The extra bounce flips the colour order

explain.say: In the main bow, the light comes back at about 42 degrees from the point opposite the Sun. Red comes out at the widest angle, so red is on the outside.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The extra bounce flips the colour order

explain.say: Some light bounces twice inside the drop before escaping. The second bounce sends it out at a bigger angle, about 51 degrees, and flips the colours, so red is on the inside.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The extra bounce flips the colour order

explain.say: Light leaks out at every bounce, so the second bow is fainter. And no light from either bow reaches you from the gap between them, which is why that band of sky looks darker.

faq.q: Why are the colours of a double rainbow flipped?
faq.a: The second rainbow comes from light that reflects twice inside each raindrop. The extra reflection turns the light around once more, so the colour order is reversed, with red on the inside.
asks: Why is the second rainbow upside down?
Why is red inside the top rainbow?

faq.q: Why is the second rainbow fainter?
faq.a: Every time light hits the back of a raindrop, some escapes instead of reflecting. Light for the second bow reflects twice, so more is lost and the bow is dimmer.
asks: Why is the outer rainbow dim?
Why can I hardly see the second rainbow?

faq.q: Why is the sky darker between two rainbows?
faq.a: Raindrops in that band send no light from either the first or second bow towards you, so it looks darker than the sky around it. It is called Alexander's dark band.
asks: Why is there a dark strip between rainbows?

faq.a: You see rainbow light from every raindrop at the same angle, about 42 degrees, from the point directly opposite the Sun. All the points at the same angle make a circle, and the ground hides the lower part.
asks: Why is a rainbow an arc?
Can a rainbow be a full circle?

faq.q: When can I see a double rainbow?
faq.a: You need the Sun low behind you and rain falling in front, often in the early morning or late afternoon after a shower. Big raindrops and bright sunshine make the second bow easier to see.
asks: Where should I look for a rainbow?
What time of day are rainbows?

facts: The main rainbow has a radius of about 42 degrees around the point opposite the Sun; the secondary bow is at about 50 to 53 degrees.
The darker band between the two bows is named Alexander's dark band after Alexander of Aphrodisias, who described it around 200 CE.

quiz.say: In the second, outer rainbow of a double rainbow, where is the red?
quiz.show: In the outer rainbow, red is…

options.show: On the outside, like the main bow
options.say: On the outside, like the main bow

quiz.why: Light for the outer bow reflects twice inside the drops, which reverses the colour order, so red is on the inside.
